summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 2 in Infectum (Jan 2.33/5437)

data.turoyo: Aṯino ʕal i arʕo, droʕi, haṯe iḏi qayiṯo harke. Haṯe qayiṯo harke hawxa, xəd i ʕade, xəd maydəd hawxa qurfatla w maḥtatla harke.
data.translation: I came down onto the ground; my arm, this hand of mine was stuck here. It was stuck here like this, as usual, as when you fold it like this and put it here.

rationale: First example of new bending/folding sense; ordinary arm-position context rules out treating the gesture as literal fracture.

summary: New sense 1b: (fig., Detrans.) körperlich gebrochen, erschöpft sein;
rationale: The already printed 113/97 describes a woman after childbirth as qrəfto and məṯto, without a literal skeletal fracture. Assign a figurative subsense to this existing example; one attestation.

summary: New sense 2: to bend, fold (a limb)
rationale: The arm/hand is positioned xəd i ʕade and then put here (maḥtatla harke). Ordinary deliberate folding is not breaking the limb. One clear demonstrative passage; compare the inherited Detransitive ant-riddle bending without assuming it proves active fracture.

data.translation: Der Prinz kam eines Tages mit dem Pferdeknecht, sie brachten das Pferd an das Ufer des Sees, es schaute hinein, wich zurück und lief davon. Beinahe hätte es seinem Wärter noch den Hals gebrochen.

rationale: Thin active Preterit cell; horse almost causes a neck fracture.

data.translation: Uncle Ishoʕ: Hail used to come. <...> It did not leave anyone to eat wheat, or barley, or anything. It broke it all, threw it down on the ground, threw it down.

rationale: Thin Preterit cell after round 1 (two); hail is a nonhuman causer. The cut retains both the hail antecedent and the explicit wheat/barley patients for a self-contained crop-breakage context.

summary: New idiom: b-qrafte d-qḏolo 'dass der Hals brechen möge' (Fluch)

data.headword: b-qrafte d-qḏolo 'dass der Hals brechen möge' (Fluch)
data.turoyo: Way, lo ahla w lo b xere, b qrafte d qḏolax, w aloho maṭər ʕaynax!
data.translation: Weh dir! Nicht willkommen und nicht zum Guten! Daß dir der Hals bräche und Gott dir die Augen aus dem Kopfe fliegen ließe!

rationale: Search qrafte finds the existing 66/207 nominal example and a ṭyr context, with no idiom-list headword; list the formula explicitly once. The feminine addressee and a following finite wish vary the existing context.

summary: Active breaking takes possessed body-part objects, while Detransitive makes the neck, back, tree, walnut kernel or stalk the patient participant. qrf 2 nausea is incompatible with these physical contexts.
No Preterit-wa is inferred from anterior reporting at 23/54 or the near-event expression at 113/169. gməqrofi at 92/34 has an irrealis consequence without -wa.

The inherited Detransitive sense text includes its base forms qrīf/məqrəf; that wording is retained. Its examples establish fracture and, in the ant riddle, bending/breakability. A separate figurative 1b isolates the already attested exhausted person.

The sole old active example concerns a judge breaking a pencil as a death-sentence gesture; its translation reflects the whole action. The new physical body-part evidence broadens the active gloss without rewriting this inherited example.
Lookup qrofo found no existing quotation; qrafte was already attested in this root and incidentally under ṭyr. The curse is now explicitly listed in Idiomatic phrases.
Round 1 already supplied active Infectum and Infinitiv. The reader’s missing-Infectum claim at Jan 2.33/5437 therefore does not justify a new box; what is new is nonfracturing active folding.
The two hail contexts instantiate the same literal crop breakage. Select the passage with an explicit hail antecedent rather than repeat a pronoun-only destruction sequence.

The inherited Detransitive ant-riddle is still ambiguous between bending and breakability, as round 1 noted. Jan supplies a clearer active human demonstration but does not authorize moving the old example to a newly reconstructed Detransitive sense.
Jan English is the project machine translation, not an edition translation. It is reproduced only as supplied and is not evidence for senses; all semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo.
Is breaking off millet conventional technical harvesting terminology, or an ordinary application of qrf? One occurrence is insufficient to decide lexical specialization.
Does Detransitive məqrəf in the ant riddle mean bending without fracture, or potential breakage? The inherited translation and gloss are retained.
Confirm PrS numbering of the fox’s broken back (supplied 67/101 versus inherited prs 193/1); no duplicate is added.
Confirm the active bending/folding reading of qurfatla at Jan 2.33/5437 and whether a joint is merely flexed; the context supports ordinary positioning, but no recording or gesture was available.
Millet as object of qrofo is an agricultural application of breaking off; whether it is conventional technical terminology remains open.
Hail breaks crop growth; this supports round 1 broadening from pencil to body parts/crops, without a separate weather-destruction sense.
